parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
$\mathbf{W}$ can be formed by reacting $\text{HOCH}_2\text{COOH}$ with an excess of $\text{SOCl}_2$.

Write an equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Once $\mathbf{W}$ and $\mathbf{X}$ have reacted together, an excess of $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa(aq)}$ is added to the reaction mixture.

Suggest why.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The reaction of $\mathbf{W}$ with $\mathbf{X}$, reaction 1, follows an addition-elimination mechanism. Complete the mechanism for the reaction of **W** with **X**. Include all relevant curly arrows, lone pairs of electrons, charges and partial charges. Use $\text{Ar-NH}_2$ to represent **X**.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
$(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{NH}$ reacts with $\mathbf{Y}$ in reaction 2.

Explain why $(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{NH}$ can act as a nucleophile.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem:
The purity of lidocaine can be checked using thin-layer chromatography. Ethyl ethanoate is used as the solvent.

The $R_{\text{f}}$ values of $\mathbf{X}$ and lidocaine are given in Table 6.1.
Table 6.1

| compound | $R_{\text{f}}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\mathbf{X}$ | 0.49 |
| lidocaine | 0.71 |

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Identify the substances used as the mobile and stationary phases in this thin-layer chromatography experiment.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: State how an $R_{\text{f}}$ value can be calculated.

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest why the $R_{\text{f}}$ value for $\mathbf{X}$ is less than that for lidocaine.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem:
A proton ($^{1}\text{H}$) NMR spectrum of lidocaine is shown in Fig. 6.2. 
Fig. 6.2
Table 6.2

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

Fig. 6.2

| environment of proton | example | chemical shift range $\delta / \text{ppm}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| alkane | $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{CH}_2-$, $>\text{CH}-$ | 0.9-1.7 |
| alkyl next to C=O | $\text{CH}_3-\text{C=O}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{C=O}$, $>\text{CH}-\text{C=O}$ | 2.2-3.0 |
| alkyl next to aromatic ring | $\text{CH}_3-\text{Ar}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{Ar}$, $>\text{CH}-\text{Ar}$ | 2.3-3.0 |
| alkyl next to electronegative atom | $\text{CH}_3-\text{O}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{O}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$ | 3.2-4.0 |
| attached to alkene | $=\text{CHR}$ | 4.5-6.0 |
| attached to aromatic ring | $\text{H}-\text{Ar}$ | 6.0-9.0 |
| aldehyde | $\text{HCOR}$ | 9.3-10.5 |
| alcohol | $\text{ROH}$ | 0.5-6.0 |
| phenol | $\text{Ar}-\text{OH}$ | 4.5-7.0 |
| carboxylic acid | $\text{RCOOH}$ | 9.0-13.0 |
| alkyl amine | $\text{R}-\text{NH}-$ | 1.0-5.0 |
| aryl amine | $\text{Ar}-\text{NH}_2$ | 3.0-6.0 |
| amide | $\text{RCONHR}$ | 5.0-12.0 |

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.text: Predict the splitting patterns of the peaks at $\delta$ 2.6 and $\delta$ 1.1.

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text:
The ratio of the areas under the peaks at $\delta$ 3.0 and $\delta$ 2.3 is 1:3 respectively.

Identify the protons in the $^{1}\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of lidocaine that are responsible for the peaks at these chemical shift values.

parts.label: (f)(iii)
parts.text: Predict the number of peaks in the carbon-13 ($^{13}\text{C}$) NMR spectrum of lidocaine.
